entries.title: Two ways to see Mount Fuji

state.brief: Help readers compare two views of Mount Fuji and find the original museum records.

content.headline: Two ways to see Mount Fuji
content.sub: In one print, a breaking wave almost hides Mount Fuji. In the other, the mountain fills the frame. Katsushika Hokusai made both views for the same series.
content.cta: View The Great Wave at The Met

features.title: Look through the wave
features.body: Follow the curve of the water down to the white peak between the boats. The distant mountain is smaller than the crest in the foreground.

features.title: Read the slope
features.body: In South Wind, Clear Sky, the long diagonal of Mount Fuji carries the eye across the print. Small clouds give the open sky its scale.

page.imageAlt: A curling blue wave towers over three boats, with a small, snow-capped Mount Fuji visible beyond.
page.imageCredit: Katsushika Hokusai, ca. 1830–32. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, H. O. Havemeyer Collection, Bequest of Mrs. H. O. Havemeyer, 1929 (JP1847). Open Access, CC0.

relatedStory.title: A closer look at Red Fuji
relatedStory.imageAlt: A rust-red Mount Fuji rises above a line of trees beneath a blue sky streaked with white clouds.
relatedStory.imageCredit: Katsushika Hokusai, ca. 1830–32. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Henry L. Phillips Collection, Bequest of Henry L. Phillips, 1939 (JP2960). Open Access, CC0.
